portInfo.description: Cartagena’s best compact route connects named places rather than promising the entire historic centre:the Clock Tower/Portal de los Dulces, San Pedro Claver and Las Bóvedas. Castillo San Felipe adds a distinct hill-fort visit outside that street circuit. Heat makes a shaded lunch and fewer paid interiors sensible. The official tourism article’s generic “on foot at any time” phrasing is not a safety guarantee or an accessible-route audit. Port Oasis occupies part of the cruise-terminal campus and limits access to arriving/embarking cruise guests. Its animal-recovery/conservation role is described by the operator, but undated animal counts are not repackaged as current wildlife statistics. Its internal location can support a short call without a traffic-dependent island excursion.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Port Oasis Ecopark, Port Oasis inside Cartagena Cruise Terminal, Manga, Cartagena: A close-to-ship garden and animal-recovery/conservation setting. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Restricted to arriving/embarking cruise guests; not public access and no guaranteed animal sightings.

Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, Castillo San Felipe, Cartagena de Indias: A separate military-history visit beyond the old-city street loop. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). Slopes, tunnels and sun exposure; confirm current ticket/accessible portions.

Torre del Reloj and Portal de los Dulces, Clock Tower and adjacent Portal de los Dulces, walled-city entrance, Cartagena: A defined meeting point and local sweets/architecture stop. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Agree exactly which side of the gate your driver uses.

San Pedro Claver church, Parroquia San Pedro Claver, walled city, Cartagena: A working religious landmark with historical interpretation. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Church/museum admission and worship restrictions must be checked separately.

Las Bóvedas, Between Santa Clara and Santa Catalina forts, northern walled city, Cartagena: Vaulted military/prison architecture now associated with crafts and shops. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Retail activity does not guarantee every gallery opens at your visit time.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Have the driver write the city meeting point and the actual Manga terminal destination. Being back at the Clock Tower is not being back at the ship.
